newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CARDINALS TAKE 2-0 LEAD OVER PADRES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CARDINALS TAKE 2-0 LEAD OVER PADRES.

text.p: Tom Pagnozzi's eighth-inning grounder off pitcher Trevor Hoffman's glove scored Brian Jordan with the leading run to give the St. Louis Cardinals a 2-0 lead in the National League Division Series Thursday.
St. Louis can clinch its first trip to the NL Championship Series since 1987 with a victory at San Diego Saturday.

Doug Bochtler issued a leadoff walk to Brian Jordan in the eighth and he advanced to second on Gary Gaetti's groundout. John Mabry was intentionally walked and both runners moved up when Bochtler uncorked a wild pitch.

Hoffman relieved and Pagnozzi hit a soft line drive that Hoffman tried to avoid. He got a glove on it, but it struck the ground as Jordan dashed home. Second baseman Jody Reed recovered to throw Pagnozzi out at first.
Rick Honeycutt (1-0) pitched a scoreless eighth for the win before Dennis Eckersley recorded his second save in as many games with a nine-pitch ninth. It was Eckersley's 13th career post-season save.
San Diego rallied from a 4-1 deficit with two runs in the sixth and one in the eighth.

St. Louis opened the scoring in the third. Luis Alicea drew a leadoff walk from starter Scott Sanders and was sacrificed to second by Benes. Ozzie Smith walked before McGee hit the next pitch into centre field, scoring Alicea with the game's first run.

Ken Caminiti, who had failed to put the ball in play in his first five at-bats in the series with four strikeouts and a walk, led off the fifth with a 392-foot blast over the right-field wall to tie the game.

Andy Benes, a former Padre, retired the first 12 batters he faced, striking out six, before Caminiti hit his first career post-season homer. Benes allowed four runs and six hits in seven-plus innings with a walk and nine strikeouts.

But the Cardinals struck back for three runs in their half of the fifth. Benes had a one-out single and Smith followed with a single. Willie McGee walked to load the bases, chasing Sanders for Dario Veras. Five pitches later, Ron Gant belted a 2-2 pitch over the head of Finley in centre, clearing the bases for a 4-1 St. Louis lead.
Gant said Brian Jordan, who was on deck, "told me just swing straight and swing hard."
After fouling off the first pitch, "I took an easier swing on the hit and drove the ball over his head," Gant said. "You've got to hit the ball pretty hard to get it over Finley's head."
Padres' manager Bruce Bochy said: "We made a mistake on that. Steve Finley is a gold glove outfielder and something went wrong there."
The heart of the San Diego lineup -- Finley, Caminiti and Wally Joyner -- is a combined 3-for-20 in the series with one RBI. The Padres are 2-for-12 with runners in scoring position.
